reason: The link is real, but §504 gives only the title 'the New Adam' (with 1 Cor 15:47) and no prefigure/figure wording, so it is preparatory at most. Types and category are right.
'By her obedience she became the new Eve, mother of the living' is a typological title, not figure language. The link is real but preparatory.

§522 says all the 'rituals and sacrifices, figures and symbols' of the First Covenant converge on Christ, a general statement that fits a TEACHES row for ceremonial-law. The word 'sacrifices' would equally support a TEACHES row for `ot-sacrifices`.

'In the spirit and power of Elijah' (Lk 1:17) makes John Elijah's likeness but uses no figure wording, so it is not explicit. The person-to-person link is real (cf. §719, 'the cycle of prophets begun by Elijah'), so label it preparatory.

'This sign prefigures that circumcision of Christ which is Baptism' is explicit. 'This sign' is circumcision as the rite of incorporation into Abraham's descendants, which Jesus received, so the OT rite is the right Type.

'Recalls the exodus and presents him as the definitive liberator' treats the exodus as a provisional deliverance that Christ surpasses. Preparatory is the right label because the text has no figure wording.

The antithetical Adam/Christ link is plain ('the new Adam who remained faithful just where the first Adam had given in'), and §538 says the temptations 'recapitulate' Adam's. But the text has no figure wording, so label it preparatory.

The link and the preparatory label hold ('Jesus fulfills Israel's vocation'; §538: the temptations 'recapitulate ... the temptations of Israel in the desert'). But what is fulfilled is Israel's forty years of testing as God's son, not its disobedience, which is only the contrast. The Type should be a new 'Israel's Forty Years of Testing in the Wilderness' (Deut 8:2-3, the texts Jesus answers Satan with) rather than this Type, whose description is the 1 Cor 10 warning.

'The Daughter of Zion, a figure of his Church' is explicit wording, and the Type (Jerusalem/the people of God personified, Zech 9:9 in the context of the entry) is the figure the text names. Ecclesial is right.

§580 says 'Jesus fulfills the Law' and that the Law now lies 'upon the heart' of the Servant, so preparatory is right. A stronger quote would be 'Jesus fulfills the Law to the point of taking upon himself the curse of the Law'.
The Sinai/Mount of the Beatitudes parallel and 'did not abolish the Law but fulfilled it' carry the link from the Law to the New Covenant. Preparatory and Covenantal are right.

'Jesus perfects the dietary law ... by revealing its pedagogical meaning' presents the food laws as teaching purity of heart ('from within, out of the heart'), so preparatory fits. Ecclesial matches the existing edge; Covenantal (the interiority of the New Law) would be equally defensible.

'Identified himself with the Temple by presenting himself as God's definitive dwelling-place' does link the Temple to Christ, but it has no figure wording. The explicit warrant for this pair is §593 ('The Temple prefigures his own mystery'), so label this one preparatory.
'Jesus did not abolish the Law of Sinai, but rather fulfilled it' is fulfilment wording. Preparatory and Christological are right.
'The Temple prefigures his own mystery ... his Body would be the definitive Temple' is explicit, and Christ is the right antitype.

The link is real, but the text calls Jesus 'the Paschal Lamb' as a title. 'Symbol' there describes the lamb as the sign of Israel's redemption, not as a figure of Christ, so label it preparatory. Note that the 'suffering Servant ... led to the slaughter' half of the sentence is Isaiah 53 prophecy, not typology.

'Christ's death is both the Paschal sacrifice that accomplishes the definitive redemption' presents the Passover as provisional and fulfilled in the Cross, but it has no figure wording, so label it preparatory. `christs-passion` is the right precision for the antitype.
'It completes and surpasses all other sacrifices' is fulfilment language. Preparatory and the pair `ot-sacrifices` → `christs-passion` are right.

Christ 'entered, not into a sanctuary made by human hands ... but into heaven itself' contrasts the sanctuary the high priest entered with heaven, a surpassing that fits preparatory. The text describes the OT Type without naming it (the words of Heb 9:24 left out by the ellipsis call it 'a copy of the true one'), so this is borderline.

'Several anointed ones of the Lord in the Old Covenant, pre-eminently King David. But Jesus is God's Anointed in a unique way' makes David the chief of the lesser anointed ones, surpassed by Christ, so preparatory fits. The same sentence also supports `anointing-of-kings-priests-and-prophets` → `christ`.

'This event was a figure of the fire of the Holy Spirit' is explicit, and the event is the fire from heaven on the Carmel sacrifice. The text's antitype is the Spirit's transforming fire in general; Pentecost ('tongues as of fire') is the paragraph's own instance and the nearest existing Type, so it is acceptable.

'In the Holy Spirit, Christ fulfills these figures' is explicit, and the figures are the clouds of the theophanies (Sinai, the tent, the desert, Solomon's Temple), so the claim depends on the td-003 broadening. The paragraph also names the fulfilments (the overshadowing of Mary, the Transfiguration cloud, the Ascension), which the reviewer may want as further links.

'If God's law was written on tablets of stone ... then the letter from Christ ... not on tablets of stone, but on tablets of human hearts' sets the Law of Sinai below the New Covenant written by the Spirit (2 Cor 3:3). Preparatory and Covenantal fit.
'The flood, whose symbolism refers to Baptism' states the flood's figurative meaning outright. 'Symbolism' here is figure language, so explicit stands.

The paragraph sets Noah's dove beside the dove at Jesus' baptism under the heading 'The dove', but it states no fulfilment or figure between them. The link rests only on that juxtaposition, so label it synthesized; the next sentence ('remains in the purified hearts of the baptized') equally supports the existing `the-dove-and-the-olive-branch-noah` → `baptism`.
'God gave the Law as a pedagogue to lead his people towards Christ' (Gal 3:24) is a clear statement that the Law prepared the way. Preparatory is right.

'The Remnant of the poor that returns from the Exile is one of the most transparent prefigurations of the Church' is explicit. The figure is the returning remnant, a people, which the existing description ('the restored holy people returning') matches; `the-faithful-remnant` would also fit.

'The Exile already stands in the shadow of the Cross' is anticipation, not prefigure/figure wording, so label it preparatory. The pair itself is right: the Exile as a death and purification that opens a restoration.
pastoral_flag: The catalog description of `the-babylonian-exile` ('a figure of the long desolation the Jews endured after rejecting Christ') is a collective claim §710 does not make. §710 reads the Exile as God's 'mysterious fidelity' and Israel's purification, so make the description neutral before this link carries it.

reason: §711 teaches directly about 'the small Remnant, the people of the poor, who await in hope', so a TEACHES row for `the-faithful-remnant` fits.

'John is Elijah who must come' fulfils Malachi's prophecy (Mal 4:5; Mt 17:11), and prophecy is not typology. The typological ground is the next sentence: the fire of the Spirit that was in Elijah (§696) now dwells in John. The link is real but preparatory, not explicit.

§721 names no OT figure fulfilled in Mary. It reports that Tradition has 'read the most beautiful texts on wisdom in relation to Mary', which is a liturgical use of texts, and 'Seat of Wisdom' makes her the dwelling of Wisdom (Christ, 1 Cor 1:24), not Wisdom's antitype. At most this is a TEACHES row; a link, if wanted, would be Wisdom's dwelling place (Sir 24:8-12) → Mary, synthesized.

Gabriel greeting her as 'Daughter of Zion': 'Rejoice' (Zeph 3:14; Lk 1:28) is a typological title with no figure wording, so the link is real but preparatory. The 'Rejoice' oracle itself is prophecy; the Type is the personified people of Zion.

'She is the burning bush of the definitive theophany' is a strong typological identification, but it is a title without figure wording, so label it preparatory. The Type and the Marian category are right.
'Mary became the Woman, the new Eve (mother of the living)' is a title without figure wording. Label it preparatory, as with §511.

§697 itself groups the clouds of the theophanies (Sinai, the tent of meeting, the desert, Solomon's Temple) as 'these figures', so broadening the Type follows the Catechism's own grouping. All four links still read true because the description keeps the exodus pillar, though the → baptism (1 Cor 10:2) and → `the-holy-spirit-as-divine-guide` links rest on the pillar specifically; verse memberships should add Exod 24:15-18, 40:34-38 and 1 Kgs 8:10-11.
A concrete NT event, distinct from the sacrament of Baptism, with an accurate description (Matt 3:13-17). §701 and the held §§536 and 556 rows need it.

A concrete NT event that §538–540 treat at length ('recapitulate the temptations of Adam ... and of Israel in the desert'), and the description is accurate. It is the right antitype for the Israel-in-the-wilderness link, with that Type revised as I suggest for c539.

§559 calls the Daughter of Zion 'a figure of his Church' and §722 gives Mary the title, and the description is plain and Scripture-first. It rightly makes the Type the personified people of Zion, not the oracles addressed to her.

Its only link (§721) does not hold as typology: the Catechism reports a liturgical reading of wisdom texts 'in relation to Mary' and calls her 'Seat of Wisdom', the dwelling of Wisdom rather than its antitype. Personified Wisdom is also a literary personification, not a concrete OT person, event or institution.
